title: The -jon/-jen Form: Talking About What Should Happen

sections.title: The third person of a form you already know
sections.content: You already build commands with -j (*menj!*) and "let's" with -junk/-jünk (*induljunk!*) — both are the same imperative-subjunctive suffix, just for different persons. -jon/-jen extends that same suffix to "he/she/it/they should...", following vowel harmony (-jon back, -jen front, -jön for rounded front) and the same consonant-assimilation rules you already know from *menj* → *menjen*, *tesz* → *tegyen*.

sections.title: From te/mi to ő
rows: let's set off → (that) he/she set(s) off

sections.title: Also the formal "you", the same way as szeretne

items.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine. (formal "you")

sections.content: This is also how you address a stranger formally, the way you already used *szeretne* and *tudna* — *Foglaljon helyet!* ("Have a seat", to a stranger) uses exactly this ending, just on a different verb each time.
